key_insight: A synchronization-theoretic autoencoder can map cylinder–airfoil wake interactions to a low-order oscillator model and predict oscillation death, where vortex shedding is suppressed by body-body coupling.
engineering_relevance: This provides a data-driven way to assess flow stability and interaction effects in paired aerodynamic components, supporting design of quieter or more stable fluid machinery.
method: Direct numerical simulation of 2D incompressible cylinder–airfoil flows at Reynolds number 100
Parameter sweep over streamwise gap Δx, vertical offset Δy, and airfoil angle of attack α to identify four vortex-shedding regimes
Train a synchronization-theoretic autoencoder on aerodynamic coefficients to infer a coupled-oscillator representation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports four distinct flow regimes from the parameter sweep and a theoretical stability prediction on a learned low-order coordinate that matches suppressed vortex shedding behavior.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated only for 2D, low-Reynolds-number cases, so generalization to higher-Re flows or 3D geometries may require retraining and validation.
paper_title: Studying oscillation death in two-dimensional cylinder-airfoil interactions with synchronization-theoretic autoencoder
